To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the microbial biomass and CLPP of soils amended with maize litter changed significantly during the decomposition process and that the CLPP of soils with decomposing maize litter was similar after 52 weeks of decomposition.
the CLPP of soil bacteria changed with the decomposition of maize residues and that the CLPP from different soil management systems were very similar after 52 weeks of decomposition.
(1) microbial biomass C decreased during the decomposition process, and (2) the utilization of carbohydrates decreased during decomposition, and amino acid utilization increased.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the effects of litter decomposition on microbial community structure and function, and how the soil management system affects this process.
the decomposition process of maize litter under two soil management types.
the effects of maize litter decomposition on microbial biomass C, basal respiration and community level physiological profile of soil bacteria in soils under different soil management types.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the CLPP of soil bacteria is influenced by soil management type and by the decomposition of maize residues.
the microbial community in soils with incorporated litter is more similar to the control soil without litter, than the microbial community in the soils with mulched litter.

decomposition of maize litter significantly changed soil microbial biomass, basal resirpation, and community level metabolic profiles, but the changes were similar for the different soil management types.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

maize litter decomposition was characterized by a decrease in the relative utilization of carbon sources with high molecular weight and an increase of the utilization of carbon sources of low molecular weight.
the microbial community was stimulated during the decomposition of the maize litter and the microbial community shifted from a carbohydrate to a protein-based community.
the decomposition of maize residues had a significant influence on the CLPP of soil microorganisms.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the decomposition of maize residues in soil leads to a shift in CLPP towards amino acid utilization.
microbial biomass, respiration, and CLPP are all affected by the addition of maize litter, and that the effect is not dependent on soil type.
the microbial community was able to adapt to the new conditions created by the addition of maize litter and the shift in the CLP profiles was similar in all soils.
